mainTopic: Must adults stop a קטן from doing an איסור? A series of proofs and rejections, and the meaning of 'warning adults about minors.'
overview: The עמוד asks whether a בית דין must stop a קטן who does an איסור on his own. רבי פדת's advice to let children find lost keys on שבת suggests the answer is no. A ברייתא seems to support him, but אביי pushes it off: that case involves only rabbinic איסורים. A ברייתא about a child putting out a fire seems to say we must stop him. רבי יוחנן answers that the child there acts for his father, unlike a גוי, who acts for himself. Next comes a ברייתא about a חבר's son eating at his עם הארץ grandfather's house. רבי יוחנן pushes it off as דמאי, and the גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן was unsure and simply pushed off each proof. Further proofs are also pushed off: from impure תרומה, answered as rabbinic תרומה, and from a baby nursing from a non-kosher source, answered as a case of danger. Along the way the גמרא explains אבא שאול's custom of nursing from an animal on יום טוב. Finally, three פסוקים that warn adults about minors are each read as forbidding only actively giving a child the איסור. The גמרא then begins to explain why all three פסוקים are needed, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Send children to look for the lost keys
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדת finishes his advice: let boys and girls walk where the keys were lost, and if they find them, they will bring them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bring boys and girls and let them walk around there. If they find the keys, they will bring them back.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רבי פדת's practical advice from the previous עמוד about keys lost in the public street on שבת. He says not to ask anyone to carry them, but to let children wander there, and they may bring the keys on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children are never told to carry anything. They are just placed where the keys are. If they pick up the keys and carry them home on their own, an adult is allowed to let that happen.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them walk or wander around

phrases.english: and lead boys and girls
phrases.notes: This continues from the previous עמוד. Someone lost keys in the street on שבת, and רבי פדת is giving him advice.

phrases.english: and let them walk around there,
for if they find them,
they will bring them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ruling that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An adult may place children where they could find and carry the keys, as long as he does not tell them to carry.

steps.title: What this shows about stopping a child from sinning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי פדת holds a בית דין is not required to stop a קטן who eats נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems רבי פדת holds that if a child eats non-kosher meat, בית דין does not have to stop him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule out of רבי פדת's advice. If we may let children carry on שבת, then it seems we do not have to stop a child who does an איסור on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פדת's advice only works if adults have no duty to stop children from doing an איסור. The גמרא turns his specific case into a general position: a קטן אוכל נבלות, אין בית דין מצווין להפרישו. The rest of the section tests this position.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child under the age of מצוות
Meat of animals that were not slaughtered properly
To separate him from the איסור, to stop him

steps.whatToRemember: The key question of this section: must בית דין stop a קטן who is doing an איסור? According to רבי פדת, no.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about telling a child to do an איסור. Everyone agrees that is forbidden. The question is only whether we must stop a child who does it on his own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic question in the laws of חינוך: how responsible are adults for what children do on their own?

phrases.english: Apparently, he holds:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי פדת, who gave the advice about the keys.

phrases.english: a minor who eats meat of unslaughtered animals —
the court is not commanded to stop him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general halachic position out of the advice in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי פדת holds that בית דין does not have to stop a קטן from doing an איסור.

steps.title: Support from a ברייתא about a child on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests support: we may not tell a child to bring a key or a seal, but we may let him pick plants and throw on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? A person should not tell a child, 'Bring me a key' or 'Bring me a seal.' But he may let the child pick plants and let him throw things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to back up רבי פדת. It forbids telling a child to do a מלאכה, but allows letting him do one on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws the same line as רבי פדת: giving an order is forbidden, but doing nothing while the child acts is allowed. If we may let a child pick plants and throw on שבת, it seems we do not have to stop him from an איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
A person should not say to a child
'Bring me a key,' 'Bring me a seal,'
but he may let him pick plants,
he may let him throw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the inference in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין does not have to stop a קטן from doing an איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lets a child pick plants and throw on שבת, while forbidding anyone to tell him to bring something.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא may only involve rabbinic איסורים
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: the picking is from a pot without a hole, and the throwing is into a כרמלית. Both are only rabbinic איסורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'Picking' means from a pot that has no hole. 'Throwing' means into a כרמלית, which is only forbidden by the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows that the ברייתא does not prove רבי פדת's view. The child in the ברייתא may only be breaking rabbinic rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking from a pot without a hole and throwing into a כרמלית are both איסורים דרבנן. Maybe we do not have to stop a child from a rabbinic איסור, but we still must stop him from a Torah איסור like eating נבלות. So the ברייתא cannot prove the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A flowerpot without a hole; picking from it is only a rabbinic איסור
An in-between area, neither fully public nor private; carrying there is only rabbinically forbidden
Of the רבנן; a rabbinic rule, not a Torah rule

phrases.english: אביי said:
'Picks' — from a pot that has no hole,
'Throws' — into a כרמלית, which is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי תּוֹלֵשׁ בְּעָצִיץ שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבי פדת's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may deal only with rabbinic איסורים, so it says nothing about Torah איסורים like נבלות.

steps.title: Challenge: we tell a child not to put out a fire
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says we say nothing to a גוי who comes to put out a fire on שבת, but we tell a Jewish child 'do not put it out,' because his rest is our responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a גוי comes to put out a fire, we do not tell him 'put it out' or 'don't put it out,' because his resting on שבת is not our responsibility. If a child comes to put out a fire, we tell him 'don't put it out,' because his resting is our responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רבי פדת. It says we must stop a Jewish child from putting out a fire on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting out a fire is a Torah-level מלאכה. The ברייתא says a child's שבת rest is our responsibility, so we must stop him. That suggests בית דין must stop a קטן from an איסור, against רבי פדת.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; brings a source
His resting on שבת is their responsibility

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A non-Jew who comes to put out a fire —
we do not say to him 'put it out' or 'do not put it out,'
because his resting is not their responsibility.
A child who comes to put out a fire —
we say to him 'do not put it out,'
because his resting is their responsibility.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the support in steps 3-4 was rejected, the גמרא now brings a source that seems to contradict רבי פדת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי פדת's view that בית דין does not have to stop a קטן from an איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires stopping a Jewish child from a Torah-level מלאכה on שבת, so we do have to stop a קטן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the child is acting for his father
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the ברייתא is about a child who puts out the fire for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The ברייתא is about a child who is acting with his father's consent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. The child in the ברייתא is not acting on his own. He is putting out the fire for his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the child acts for his father, it is as if the adult is having the מלאכה done for him, and that is forbidden. A child acting purely for himself is a different case, so רבי פדת's view still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: With his father's consent; acting on his father's behalf

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
It is about one who acts with his father's consent,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּעוֹשֶׂה עַל דַּעַת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say we must stop any child doing an איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: We must stop him only when he is acting for his father. A child acting for himself does not have to be stopped.

steps.title: Then a גוי acting for a Jew should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a גוי who puts out the fire is also doing it for the Jew. Is that allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to a גוי. He is also acting with the Jew's consent. Is that allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. If acting for someone is the problem, the גוי in the same ברייתא is also acting for the Jew, yet we do not stop him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says we do not have to tell the גוי anything. But the גוי is putting out the Jew's fire, so he is also acting for the Jew. Why is that not forbidden like the child?

phrases.english: The same case regarding a non-Jew
who acts with the Jew's consent,
is it allowed?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְווֹתֵיהּ גַּבֵּי גּוֹי דְּעוֹשֶׂה עַל דַּעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation that the child is acting for his father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If acting for someone else makes it forbidden, then a גוי acting for the Jew should also be forbidden. Yet the ברייתא lets him continue.

steps.title: A גוי acts for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a גוי acts on his own decision, not on the Jew's behalf.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גוי acts according to his own wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A גוי is considered to be acting for himself, so he is not seen as the Jew's agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child naturally does what his father wants, so his act counts as being for the father. A grown גוי makes his own choices, so even if the Jew benefits, the act is his own. That is why the ברייתא treats them differently, and רבי יוחנן's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: On his own mind; by his own decision

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן pushes off the fire ברייתא by saying the child there was acting for his father, and a גוי always counts as acting for himself. Step 12 shows this was only a way to push off the proof, not a firm ruling, because רבי יוחנן was unsure about the question.

phrases.english: A non-Jew acts on his own mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי putting out a Jew's fire seemed to be acting for the Jew, just like the child acting for his father.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי decides for himself, so his act is not counted as the Jew's. A child follows his father's wishes, so his act is counted as the father's.

steps.title: The son of a חבר eating at his grandfather's house
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a חבר's son may eat at his עם הארץ grandfather's house, and if fruit is found in his hand, the father does not need to act. This seems to prove we need not stop a child from eating forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the son of a חבר often goes to his mother's father, who is an עם הארץ. We do not worry that the grandfather will feed him untithed food. If the father finds fruit in the boy's hand, he does not need to deal with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to try to prove that we do not have to stop a child from eating forbidden food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is not trusted to tithe, so his food may be untithed. Yet the ברייתא lets the child eat it and does not require the father to take the fruit away. That seems to show there is no duty to separate a child from איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
A person who is careful about tithes and purity
An unlearned person who is not trusted with tithes
Fixed up, meaning tithed and permitted to eat
He does not need to deal with him

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The son of a חבר who is used to going
to his mother's father, who is an עם הארץ
we are not concerned that perhaps he will feed him
things that are not tithed.
If he found fruit in his hand,
phrases.notes: The one finding the fruit is the boy's father, the חבר.

phrases.english: he does not need to deal with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּן חָבֵר שֶׁרָגִיל לֵילֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the fire case was resolved, the גמרא brings a new source on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That there is no duty to stop a child from eating forbidden food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a חבר's son eating at his עם הארץ grandfather's house.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the leniency is only for דמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן pushes off the proof: the חכמים were lenient here only because the food is דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: with דמאי they were lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the proof by saying the case is only about food that is doubtfully tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most עמי הארץ do tithe, so the grandfather's food is only a doubt (דמאי). Since even the איסור is just a doubt, the חכמים were lenient. This does not prove anything about a child eating food that is definitely forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
With דמאי they were lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to food that is only doubtfully forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the food was surely forbidden, but it is only דמאי, where the חכמים were lenient.

steps.title: This answer clashes with רבי יוחנן's earlier answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that definitely untithed food would need tithing, but רבי יוחנן said earlier that we only stop a child acting for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the reason is that it is דמאי, which means definitely untithed food would need tithing? But didn't רבי יוחנן say the rule is about a child acting for his father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's two answers do not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'only because it is דמאי' implies that with definitely untithed food, the father would have to act. But in step 6, רבי יוחנן said we only need to stop a child who acts for his father. Here the boy eats his grandfather's food for himself, so by that rule there should be no duty even with definitely untithed food.

keyTerms.meaning: For his father, on his father's behalf

phrases.english: So the reason is because it is דמאי,
which means definitely untithed food would need tithing?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
it is about one who acts for his father!
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's answer from step 6, about the child putting out the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דִּדְמַאי, הָא וַדַּאי בְּעָא לְעַשּׂוֹרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 10 by setting it against step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's answer that the leniency is only because of דמאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer implies there is a duty when the food is surely forbidden, even though the child is not acting for his father. This contradicts רבי יוחנן's own rule from step 6.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was unsure, so he pushed off each proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן was in doubt about the rule, so he gave a different answer to each proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן was unsure about this. In one place he pushed off the proof one way, and in another place he pushed it off another way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying רבי יוחנן never decided the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His two answers are not two firm rules that have to agree. Since he was unsure, he simply showed that each proof was not a real proof. He answered the fire case with 'acting for his father' and the grandfather case with 'דמאי.'

keyTerms.meaning: He was in doubt about it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן was unsure whether we must stop a child from eating איסור. So each of his answers only pushes off a proof; none of them is a final ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יוחנן's answers as fixed halachos that must fit together. They are only ways of pushing off proofs, because he himself had a doubt.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan
was in doubt about it,
standing here, he pushes it off;
phrases.notes: Literally 'standing here'; he means in the fire case.

phrases.english: standing here, he pushes it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the answers were only ways of pushing off proofs, not firm positions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's two answers state fixed rules that contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was unsure, so each answer only weakens a proof without making a rule.

steps.title: A כהן child and impure תרומה at his grandfather's house
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a כהן חבר's son may eat at his כהן עם הארץ grandfather's house without concern about impure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the son of a כהן who is a חבר often goes to his mother's father, a כהן who is an עם הארץ. We do not worry that the grandfather will feed him impure תרומה. If the father finds fruit in the boy's hand, he does not need to deal with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, this time about impure תרומה, to prove there is no duty to stop a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here דמאי cannot be the reason, because eating impure תרומה is a serious איסור. Yet the ברייתא still lets the child eat, which seems to prove that there is no duty to stop him.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who may eat תרומה
Impure תרומה, forbidden even to a כהן

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The son of a חבר who is a כהן, who is used to going

phrases.aramaic: אֵצֶל אֲבִי אִמּוֹ כֹּהֵן עַם הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: to his mother's father, a כהן who is an עם הארץ
we are not concerned that perhaps he will feed him
impure תרומה.
If he found fruit in his hand,
he does not need to deal with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּן חָבֵר כֹּהֵן שֶׁרָגִיל לֵילֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to step 9 where the דמאי answer does not work.
steps.raayaObject: That there is no duty to stop a child from eating forbidden food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a כהן child and impure תרומה.

steps.title: It is only rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the ברייתא is about תרומה that is only required by the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about rabbinic תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by limiting the case to rabbinic תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some תרומה is only required מדרבנן, and the איסור of eating it when impure is also only rabbinic. So the ברייתא only shows leniency with a rabbinic איסור, not with a Torah one.

keyTerms.meaning: Required by the חכמים, not by the Torah

phrases.english: It is about rabbinic תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to rabbinic תרומה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a Torah איסור, but the case may be only a rabbinic one.

steps.title: A baby nursing from a non-kosher source
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a baby may nurse from a גויה or a non-kosher animal, but one may not feed him נבלות, טרפות, שקצים or רמשים. A child may nurse even on שבת, an adult may not, and אבא שאול reports nursing from a kosher animal on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a baby may keep nursing from a גויה and from a non-kosher animal, and we do not worry that he is nursing something disgusting. But one may not feed him נבלות, טרפות, שקצים and רמשים. He may nurse from all of them even on שבת, but for an adult it is forbidden. אבא שאול says: we used to nurse from a kosher animal on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about what a baby may and may not be given, to test the same question. How the גמרא uses it continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets a baby nurse from a non-kosher source, but forbids actively feeding him forbidden foods like נבלות. It also lets a child nurse on שבת while forbidding an adult to do so. אבא שאול adds a report that people nursed from a kosher animal on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals not properly slaughtered, and animals with a fatal injury
A תנא who reports a practice

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A baby may keep on nursing
from a non-Jewish woman and from a non-kosher animal,
and we are not concerned that he is nursing something disgusting.
But one may not feed him improperly slaughtered or fatally injured animals,
non-kosher creatures or creeping animals.
And from all of them he may nurse,
even on שבת.
But for an adult it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This means nursing on שבת, even from a kosher animal.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
We used to nurse
from a kosher animal on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: יוֹנֵק תִּינוֹק וְהוֹלֵךְ מִגּוֹיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תרומה proof was pushed off, the גמרא tries another source.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether we must keep a child away from forbidden food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a baby nursing and about what one may not feed him.

steps.title: The proof: a baby may nurse from a non-kosher source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the key line in the ברייתא: we are not concerned about a baby nursing from something non-kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that we are not concerned about a baby who nurses from a non-kosher creature!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started with the ברייתא in step 15. It points to the exact words that seem to prove its point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The milk of a non-kosher animal is forbidden, yet the ברייתא lets a baby drink it. So it seems we do not need to stop a קטן from eating forbidden food.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (pointing to the key line of a source)

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
We are not concerned about one who nurses from a non-kosher creature!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That we need not stop a קטן from eating forbidden food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא allowing a baby to nurse from a non-kosher animal.

steps.title: The nursing case is about danger
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the baby is allowed to nurse only because without milk he is in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is allowed because of danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The baby may nurse because of danger to his life, not because a קטן may eat forbidden food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby must have milk to live, and saving a life overrides food prohibitions. So the ברייתא says nothing about an ordinary case where a קטן eats forbidden food.

phrases.english: There it is because of danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to a case of danger.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignored that a baby's need for milk is a matter of life and death.

steps.title: Then an adult should also be allowed
steps.stepSummary: If danger is the reason, an adult in danger should also be allowed to nurse, but the ברייתא forbids an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, an adult should also be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of danger. Danger allows an adult to eat forbidden food too, so why does the ברייתא forbid an adult?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a child and an adult differently. If danger were the whole reason, the difference makes no sense.

phrases.english: If so, an adult too should be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of danger given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the baby's permission is due to danger.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Danger allows anyone, so the ברייתא should not have forbidden an adult.

steps.title: An adult needs an expert check
steps.stepSummary: An adult is allowed only after experts check and find he is in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: An adult needs an assessment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an adult is not automatically in danger. Experts must first check him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids an adult because without a check we do not assume danger. If experts find he is in danger, he would also be allowed.

phrases.english: An adult requires an assessment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Danger allows an adult as easily as a child.
steps.terutzMaskana: An adult is allowed only after experts confirm danger.

steps.title: A child should also need an expert check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a child does not also need an expert check.
steps.simpleTranslation: A child should also need an assessment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Why is a child allowed without an expert check?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If danger must be checked for an adult, the same should be true for a child. Then the ברייתא should not allow a child to nurse without a check.

phrases.english: A child too should require an assessment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only an adult needs an expert check.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same need for a check should apply to a child.

steps.title: A baby is always in danger without milk
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: we assume any baby is in danger without milk, so no check is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: an ordinary baby is in danger when it comes to milk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that a baby needs no check. Every baby is assumed to be in danger without milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an adult we must check, but for a baby the danger is a given. So the baby may nurse right away, and the ברייתא still proves nothing about a קטן eating forbidden food in a normal case.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, son of רב יהושע

steps.whatToRemember: The baby's permission to nurse from a non-kosher animal is because of danger, so it does not prove we may let a קטן eat forbidden food.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
An ordinary baby is in danger regarding milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סְתָם תִּינוֹק מְסוּכָּן אֵצֶל חָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A baby needs a check just like an adult.
steps.terutzMaskana: A baby is always assumed to be in danger without milk.

steps.title: What case is אבא שאול talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes אבא שאול and asks: if there is danger it should be allowed on שבת too, and if not, it should be forbidden on יום טוב too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: we used to nurse from a kosher animal on יום טוב. What is the case? If there is danger, it should be allowed even on שבת. If there is no danger, it should be forbidden even on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last line of the ברייתא, אבא שאול's custom. It asks what kind of case he means, since both choices seem not to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Danger overrides שבת and יום טוב alike, so why mention only יום טוב? And with no danger, taking milk from an animal should be forbidden on both days.

keyTerms.meaning: We used to have the custom

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
We used to have the custom to nurse
from a kosher animal on a Festival.
What is the case?
If there is danger,
then even on Shabbat it should also be allowed;
and if there is no danger,
even on a Festival it should be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the proof about a קטן and examines the last line of the ברייתא from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case where nursing from an animal is allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת.

steps.title: The case is suffering, not danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אבא שאול means a case of suffering without danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where there is suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is in between: the people were suffering but not in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suffering is less than danger, so it does not override everything. This explains why there could be a difference between שבת and יום טוב. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed where there is suffering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is suffering without danger.

steps.title: Why the רבנן were stricter on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Sucking milk is only a rabbinic problem. The רבנן made a decree for שבת, which carries stoning, but not for יום טוב, which is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול holds that this is separating food in an unusual way. On שבת, whose prohibition is punished by stoning, the רבנן made a decree. On יום טוב, whose prohibition is only a לאו, the רבנן did not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why suffering allows nursing on יום טוב but not on שבת. It depends on how serious each day's מלאכה prohibition is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sucking milk from an animal is taking food out from its source, but in an unusual way, so the תורה does not forbid it, only the רבנן. Since breaking שבת carries סקילה, the רבנן were strict even in a case of suffering. For יום טוב, which is only a לאו, they did not make the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Separating food from its source (a kind of מלאכה)
In an unusual way, literally 'with the back of the hand'

steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול's custom was a case of suffering. Sucking milk is only a rabbinic problem, and the רבנן made a decree for שבת but not for יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: The milk here is from a kosher animal, so the problem is not forbidden food. The issue is doing מלאכה on שבת or יום טוב.

phrases.english: And he holds it is separating food in an unusual way.
phrases.notes: Sucking milk with the mouth is not the normal way of milking, so the תורה does not forbid it, only the רבנן.

phrases.english: On Shabbat, which is a prohibition punished by stoning,
the Rabbis made a decree;
on a Festival, which is only a negative-commandment prohibition,
the Rabbis did not make a decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 23 by explaining the difference between שבת and יום טוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining a rabbinic decree by how serious each day's prohibition is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without danger, sucking milk from an animal should be forbidden on both days.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only a rabbinic problem, decreed for שבת (סקילה) but not for יום טוב (לאו).

steps.title: Proof from the verse about creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'לא תאכלום' about שקצים, read as 'do not feed them,' which warns adults about minors. It suggests this means adults must tell children not to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Do not eat them, for they are detestable.' Read it as 'do not feed them.' This warns the adults about the minors. Doesn't this mean the adult must tell the children: Do not eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that adults must stop a קטן from eating forbidden food, using a פסוק about שקצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים read the word תאכלום ('you shall eat them') as if it said תאכילום ('you shall feed them'). That shows the Torah cares about what adults let children eat. The גמרא suggests this goes all the way: adults must actively tell children to stop.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This is how the גמרא opens a proof from a source.
A detestable creature, like a non-kosher crawling animal
Do not feed them to others
To warn the adults about the minors
Isn't it that...? The גמרא uses this to suggest how a source should be read.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different ideas here. One is not putting forbidden food into a child's hands. The other is stopping a child who is eating on his own. The whole back-and-forth is about which of these the פסוק teaches.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"You shall not eat them, for they are a detestable thing,"
read it as: do not feed them
phrases.notes: The word תֹאכְלוּם is read as if it said תַּאֲכִילוּם, 'make them eat.'

phrases.english: to warn the adults about the minors.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּאָמַר לְהוּ לֹא תֵּאכְלוּ!
phrases.english: Is it not that he must say to them: Do not eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא תֹאכְלוּם כִּי שֶׁקֶץ הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the nursing discussion ends, the גמרא brings a new proof for the main question about stopping a minor.
steps.raayaObject: That adults are obligated to stop a minor from eating forbidden food

steps.title: Rejection: the verse only forbids feeding the child directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק may only mean an adult must not actively feed the child forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means he must not feed it to him with his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The פסוק only forbids an adult from actively giving the child forbidden food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding a child yourself is an action by the adult. Stopping a child who eats on his own is a different, extra duty. The פסוק proves the first, but not the second, so the main question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: With one's own hands, by direct action

steps.whatToRemember: 'בידים' (actively doing it to the child) is not the same as having to stop the child. This answer comes back in the next two proofs.

phrases.english: No, it means that he should not feed it to him with his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 25
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof from שקצים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק can be read as forbidding only active feeding, not as requiring adults to stop the child

steps.title: Proof from the verse about blood
steps.stepSummary: A second proof: the פסוק about not eating דם also warns adults about minors. Perhaps that means adults must tell children not to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'No soul among you shall eat blood.' This warns the adults about the minors. Doesn't this mean they must tell the children: Do not eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same kind of proof again, this time from the פסוק about eating דם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כל נפש מכם' ('every soul among you') are read as including a warning to adults about children. Again the גמרא suggests this means adults must stop the children.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood, which is forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"No soul among you shall eat blood,"
to warn the adults about the minors.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּאָמְרִי לְהוּ לֹא תֵּאכְלוּ!
phrases.english: Is it not that they must say to them: Do not eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כׇּל נֶפֶשׁ מִכֶּם לֹא תֹאכַל דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a parallel proof is brought
steps.raayaObject: That adults must stop a minor from eating forbidden food

steps.title: Rejection: again, only no direct feeding
steps.stepSummary: The same answer: the פסוק may only forbid adults from actively feeding blood to children.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means they must not feed it to them with their own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof the same way it rejected the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning to adults can be fully explained as a ban on active feeding. So it does not prove a duty to stop a child who eats on his own.

phrases.english: No, it means that they should not feed it to them with their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 27
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof from דם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The warning can mean only a ban on active feeding

steps.title: Proof from the double wording about כהנים and impurity
steps.stepSummary: A third proof: the doubled words 'אמור... ואמרת' about כהנים becoming טמא come to warn adults about minors. Perhaps that means adults must tell young כהנים not to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Speak... and say.' This warns the adults about the minors. Doesn't this mean he must tell them: Do not become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof, from the פסוק telling כהנים not to become impure from a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'speak' and then 'say' again. The doubled wording is read as an extra message: adults must also take care with child כהנים. The גמרא suggests this means adults must stop the children from becoming טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Speak... and say.' The doubled wording in ויקרא 21:1 about כֹּהֲנִים

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"Speak... and say,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:1. The תורה says 'speak' and then 'say' about the same message, and that extra word is where this teaching comes from.

phrases.english: to warn adults about the minors.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּאָמַר לְהוּ לָא תִּיטַּמּוֹ!
phrases.english: Is it not that he must say to them: Do not become impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel proof, this time about טומאה instead of food
steps.raayaObject: That adults must stop a minor from doing something forbidden

steps.title: Rejection: only no making them impure directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק may only forbid adults from actively making young כהנים impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means he must not make them impure with his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the third proof with the same idea: it is only about the adult's own action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An adult may not bring a child כהן into contact with טומאה. That still does not prove the adult must stop a child who becomes טמא by himself. So all three proofs fail, and the question is still open.
steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs fail for the same reason. Each פסוק can be read as forbidding only an adult's active involvement (בידים), not as requiring adults to stop the child.

phrases.english: No, it means that he should not make them impure with his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 29
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the proof from טומאת כהנים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra wording can mean only a ban on actively making them impure

steps.title: Why all three verses are needed: starting with creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why the Torah needed all three פסוקים, starting with what we would think if we only had the one about שקצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are needed: because if it had taught us only about creeping creatures...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts to show that each of the three פסוקים teaches something the others could not, and the explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three פסוקים seem to teach the same rule: adults may not actively give minors something forbidden. The גמרא asks why one would not be enough. It will show that each case has something special, so we could not learn one from another.

keyTerms.meaning: And they are needed. The גמרא uses this word to explain why more than one source is necessary.

phrases.english: And they are all needed:
because if it had taught us only about creeping creatures,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all three proofs, the גמרא explains why all three פסוקים are needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three פסוקים (שקצים, דם, טומאה) is necessary, and none could be learned from another
